answer: A work-history thread resists Sybils: a new agent starts with no trust and must complete small, checkable tasks whose results established peers verify. Each verified task adds one link to its reputation thread, like a vine growing only with sunlight over time. A lantern of public history exposes gaps: an attacker spinning up thousands of identities must pay the full labour cost for each one, since trust cannot be bought, copied, or transferred, and fake histories are pruned when verification fails.
